card.name: Singhi Chham
card.tagline: Sikkimese Buddhist snow-lion masked dance honoring Kanchenjunga
card.profile: Singhi Chham, also called the Kanchendzonga Dance, is a snow-lion masked dance of the Bhutia people of Sikkim, in which dancers perform inside a white, bluish-maned lion costume representing the snow lion (Wikipedia). It was said to have been introduced by Chador Namgyal, the third Chogyal of Sikkim, in the 18th century, and is usually performed during the Pang Lhabsol festival (Wikipedia). Each snow lion is animated by two men, with two to four lions performing to the beat of a single drummer (Wikipedia).
card.insight: The dance carries deep religious association: the peaks of Kangchenjunga - sacred to Sikkimese people and regarded as the guardian deity of Sikkim - are believed to resemble the legendary snow lion, making the dance an act of homage to the mountain (Wikipedia; EZCC).
card.image_significance: Masked snow-lion dance of Khangchendzonga. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Sikkim (Bhutia), India.
